title: The Interpretation [of] the S[i]lence, the Fast, [the Peace], the Day, [and] the Rest; [what] they are.
teaching_text:
⟨p.46⟩
[Onc]e again the discipl[es] questioned the enli[gh]tener. They say to h[im: Re/coun]t to us of the five [le]sso[ns] that [a]re proclaimed in the [wo/r]ld, [one] being cal[le]d [...] 'the peace', another called '[the] silence', [...] another 'the day', ano[ther ... We implore you, our] father, that you may p[roclaim ...]

[...] the gatherer in [... ...] then he shall cau[se] the body [...] all the lusts of the world [...] of the body in righteousness [...] is the Pill[a]r of Gl[or]y [...] because [...] ⟨p.47⟩ [...] up to the [...]

The one they call [...] it is the [Fi]rst [M]an who dwel[ls i]n the ship of living waters [...] li]ght [...] he is c[alled ...] that they have [...] glorious [...]

[...] the enlighten[er ... cal]l it 'day' [...] uni]verse as they shall [...] in the great aeon [...] are spread in the universe, it is [...] established in the [...] and the so[u]ls [...]

Blessed is he [who ...] gives joy by [...] for ever. The great [...] remains for ever and e[ver] and ever.
gardner_synopsis: Mani provides cosmological archetypes for the ritual practices of the church.
editorial_notes: Separated Gardner’s synopsis from the translated teaching text. Removed Coptic manuscript line-number intrusions (e.g., 15, 20, 30) where they function as line markers rather than content. Removed Coptic line-break slashes “/” and rejoined words broken across them where possible (e.g., enli[gh]tener; cau[se]). Removed page/header artifacts and converted the inline manuscript page marker “(47)” to ⟨p.47⟩; inferred the starting page as ⟨p.46⟩ from the chapter’s page range (46,13–47,21). Preserved lacunae [...] and editorial restorations in square brackets as given. Some fragments remain unreconstructable due to lacunose/fragmentary OCR input.
